annotations.title: What tools exist here, and when to reach for each

bundle.description: Filter by the job you are doing. Call with no arguments first to see each bundle and its size.

category.description: Filter to one category. This is about the shape of the job, NOT about safety: 42 tools outside `write` declare `readOnlyHint: false` because reading a cold address can materialise or mint as a side effect, so `category: "read"` is not a safe-tools filter. Read each result's `annotations.readOnlyHint` for that.

name.description: Return the full descriptor for exactly this tool (input schema, runnable example, annotations), e.g. `emem_ndvi`. Use this when you already know the name and want its schema without loading the whole catalog. It SHORT-CIRCUITS: when `name` is set every other argument here is ignored, so `{name, q}` is not a search within one tool. A name this responder does not carry is not an error status, you get a body with `did_you_mean` holding up to five names that share a substring with what you asked for.

q.description: Free-text filter over tool names, titles and trigger text, e.g. `ndvi`, `cloud`, `flood`, `verify`, `token`. Plain lowercased substring over name + title + description + trigger text, not fuzzy and not stemmed: `ndvi` hits, `vegetation index` only hits tools that spell that phrase. Combines with `shape`/`bundle`/`category`/`tier` as AND, so an over-narrow combination answers with an empty catalog rather than an error.

shape.description: Filter by what the answer looks like, which is usually the real question. `scalar` is one number at one address; `raster` is a gridded field over an area; `timeseries` is a value per timestep; `vector` is a learned embedding; `identity` is a canonical name for a thing; `token` is a citation handle; `proof` checks one.

tier.description: Which slice to list. Defaults to `all`, so this tool shows the whole surface even when the endpoint advertises only the core loop, and an `extended` tool you find here is callable by name through tools/call whether or not your host listed it. Pass `core` to see only what a default connection advertises.

annotations.title: Ask a free-text question about a place

cell.description: cell64 string (alternative to `place`, use when you have one from a prior emem_locate / emem_recall response). Provide this OR `place` OR `lat`+`lng`.

include.description: Opt-in REST envelope sections. `reasoning` drops `algorithms_for_question`; add `algorithms` to keep it. The MCP projection ignores these.

include_image.description: Bundle a Sentinel-2 RGB scene URL for the resolved cell. Adds ~1-2 s on first call.

model.description: Optional. Compose an EXTRA prose answer with a named model, returned as `model_answer` beside the deterministic `answer`. It does not replace it: `answer` is synthesised from the structured fields and never calls a model, so every number in it traces to a fact_cid, and asking for a model must not turn a checkable answer into an unchecked one. `model_answer` carries provenance.class = model_output. Name it by base_model (`nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge`), by family (`cosmos3_edge`, `gemma`), or by any fragment naming exactly one of them (`cosmos`); a fragment matching several is refused and names them; an unroutable name is refused with the list of routable ones, and a routable model whose service is not answering is refused as busy or down rather than silently substituted. Cosmos is refused while its host has no GPU.

place.description: Free-text place name (e.g. "Mount Fuji", "Ashok Nagar, Ranchi"). REQUIRED unless `cell` or `lat`+`lng` is provided. Extract the noun phrase from the user's turn; the responder geocodes via OSM Nominatim.

q.description: User's natural-language question about the place (e.g. "is this neighbourhood flood-prone").

verbose.description: REST only: true adds per-algorithm formulas, band metadata and long prose. The MCP projection is small (about 7 KB) either way; the REST envelope is larger.

tools.name: emem_ask

answer.description: The prose answer. Also in the content block, which carries the MCP projection; POST /v1/ask has the full envelope.

cell.description: The cell64 the question resolved to: emem's address for the place.

spatial_trace.description: A spatial memory trace: what this responder has measured at this place, as primitives a model can reason over rather than a picture a person looks at.

absent.description: Bands this responder looked for and did not find. Absence is evidence: without it a consumer infers coverage nobody measured.

at.description: [lat, lng] of the cell, so a point has a position without a second call.

counts.description: Totals taken BEFORE any cap, so truncation can be seen rather than guessed.

layers.description: Points grouped by what kind of evidence they are: surface (what the ground is), built (what stands on it), now (what is happening there), embedding (vectors for similarity). A layer absent from this list means the question never reached that kind of evidence; a band looked for and not found is in `absent` instead.

age_s.description: How old the reading was when this answer was written.

class.description: Provenance class: direct_sensor, deterministic_index, estimator, model_output, attested_execution, human_curated, unclassified. What KIND of claim this is.

f.description: Index into `receipt.fact_cids` (or the list `_projection.fact_cids_at` names). Dereference it for the signed bytes.

value.description: The measured value, in the band's own units. `null` where the band was looked for and not found: an absence is a reading.

stage.description: Which stage of the answer grounded these readings.

annotations.title: EUDR Due Diligence Statement, polygon-in, signed Annex II envelope out

cut_off_date.description: EUDR cut-off date in ISO 8601. The regulation's value is 2020-12-31; only loss after this date counts as failure.

forest_baseline_override.description: Optional baseline override. Default 'jrc_gfc2020_v3' is the EU Commission's expected (non-binding) baseline. Acceptable: 'jrc_gfc2020_v3', 'hansen_only', 'both'.

geolocation_confidential.description: Annex II geolocation-confidentiality flag. Default false.

internal_reference_number.description: The operator's own reference, echoed verbatim into the TRACES NT envelope.

legality_module.description: Operator-chosen legality provider. Default null surfaces the explicit Article 9(1)(b) out-of-EO-scope disclaimer.

max_cells_per_plot.description: Sample budget per POLYGON plot. Omit to auto-derive from polygon area (~110 cells/ha, clamped to 51,200) so the whole plot is evaluated; EUDR plots are typically large, so do not set a small value unless you have a tight latency budget. POINT plots evaluate at 1 cell.

operator.description: Operator identity written into the due-diligence statement. Echoed verbatim; this responder does not validate it against any registry, so an EORI here is a claim by the caller, not a verified one.

plots.description: One or more plots to evaluate for EUDR compliance.

commodity_hs.description: Combined Nomenclature code (HS-6+). First 4 digits detect cattle (0102/0201/0202) for the Article 2(28) cattle exemption: cattle plots are POLYGON regardless of size.

geometry_geojson.description: GeoJSON Polygon (preferred for >4 ha) OR GeoJSON Point (≤4 ha non-cattle per Article 2(28)) OR a bare {bbox:[minlng,minlat,maxlng,maxlat]}.

scope.description: Multi-tenant scope `{user_id, agent_id, run_id, org_id}`. Here it binds the scope into the receipt's signature preimage so an offline verifier rebinds the statement to this caller; unlike on the read tools it does NOT filter what is read.
